name: Wenatchee River (Lake Wenatchee – Tumwater)
blurb: Gentle braided river out of Lake Wenatchee through Plain — easy floating with mountain views.

sections.notes: Class II river with braided channels, logjams and possible strong winds. At Plain, use Chelan PUD’s stepped river-access trail below the Beaver Valley Road bridge; scout the take-out during your shuttle because the steep carry can be difficult with a raft and the exit can be easy to miss at high water. Lake Wenatchee State Park lists a $7 daily watercraft launch fee. Check seasonal parking permits and gate hours before going.

notices.title: Scout the Plain take-out first
notices.text: The Area marker shows PUD parking beside the substation. The river exit is down a steep stepped trail on the west bank below the bridge. The dotted river course does not show the landing connection; inspect the exit and carry before launching.

notices.title: Winter parking permit changes
notices.text: Lake Wenatchee operates as a Sno-Park in winter, when a Sno-Park permit replaces the Discover Pass. Gates close at dusk; no unattended overnight vehicle parking. Check the park’s current alerts and hours.

sections.routeReview: Approximate Wenatchee River course overview. Gravel bars, logjams and changing side channels can alter the usable route. The line shows the general river bends, not landing connections, navigation or remaining-time guidance.

putInAccess.sourceName: Washington State Parks — Lake Wenatchee State Park
putInAccess.note: State Parks boat-launch GIS feature 62 confirms the facility and its coordinate. Individual imagery places that coordinate inland beside the ramp, so it is now displayed as an approximate Area instead of an exact shoreline pin. The numeric coordinate and stable ID are unchanged. The park lists a $7 daily watercraft launch fee; a Sno-Park permit replaces the Discover Pass during the winter Sno-Park season. No field-verified landing or bank claim is made.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed boat launch in Lake Wenatchee State Park’s south day-use area. Launch into the lake outlet and identify the river entrance before leaving shore. This agency feature locates the facility, not the exact water-entry point. Check park gates and the seasonal parking permit before setting your shuttle.

takeOutAccess.note: Chelan PUD confirms completed public river access. Its SEPA site plan places parking north of the substation and a steep stepped trail to the west bank below the bridge. The earlier research coordinate matches that parking/trailhead on individual imagery. This resolves the missing managing-agency evidence; it does not establish an exact landing coordinate or guarantee current trail and river conditions.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use Chelan PUD’s river-access parking on River Road beside Plain Substation, south of the Beaver Valley Road/Chumstick Highway junction. Follow the signed trail to the west bank just downstream of the bridge. Scout the steep carry and take-out before launching; this Area marker is the parking/trailhead, not the landing.

sections.notes: DO NOT MISS THE TAKE-OUT just above Tumwater Canyon, which is expert-only whitewater.
